root_cause.text:
Root cause:
The `ucan` driver allocates the control message buffer using `devm_kzalloc` tied to the parent USB device (`udev->dev`) instead of the USB interface device (`intf->dev`), causing a memory leak when the driver is unbound while the physical device remains connected.

Evidence:
The patch diff shows that `devm_kzalloc` was changed to allocate memory using `&intf->dev` instead of `&udev->dev` for `ctl_msg_buffer` in `ucan_probe()`. The commit message explains that "any device managed resources should have their lifetime tied to the interface rather than parent USB device" to avoid memory leaks when drivers are unbound.

commit 9f2d3eae88d26c29d96e42983b755940d9169cd9
Author: Jakob Unterwurzacher <jakob.unterwurzacher@theobroma-systems.com>
Date:   Wed Apr 11 18:06:42 2018 +0200

    can: ucan: add driver for Theobroma Systems UCAN devices
    
    The UCAN driver supports the microcontroller-based USB/CAN
    adapters from Theobroma Systems. There are two form-factors
    that run essentially the same firmware:
    
    * Seal: standalone USB stick ( https://www.theobroma-systems.com/seal )
    
    * Mule: int
bic_trace_step.reason: In the `ucan_probe` function, the control message buffer is allocated using `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, sizeof(union ucan_ctl_payload), GFP_KERNEL);` (around line 1431). This ties the lifetime of the allocated memory to the parent USB device (`udev->dev`) instead of the USB interface device (`intf->dev`), which leads to a memory leak when the driver is unbound while the physical device remains connected.
